newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace to end production of turboprop.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace to end production of turboprop.

text.p: British Aerospace said Thursday it would finally end production of its 30-seat Jetstream 41 turboprop aircraft by the end of this year.

Struggling against an overcrowded market which has pushed sales prices below production costs, the British aircraft manufacturer said it was losing about 1 million pounds ($1.6 million) on every J41 that left its plant in Prestwick in Scotland.
The announcement pushed up the price of British Aerospace stock by 24 1/2 pence (40 cents) to 12.50 pounds ($20.46) on trading volume of more than 1.5 million shares before midday.

"With incredible competition, it (the end of production) was a case of if and when. It is clearly being read as positive by the market," said Charles Armitage, analyst with investment bank Lehman Brothers.

British Aerospace said it would make a net provision of 250 million pounds ($409 million), after taking into account a deferred tax credit of 80 million pounds ($131 million), in the accounts for the first half of 1997 for the costs of ending J41 production and an associated reorganization.
A company spokesman said the action would improve the commercial aerospace division's performance, with potential annual cost savings of 40 million pounds ($66 million).

The end of J41 production will also lead to the loss of up to 380 jobs, the latest in a series of job cuts that British Aerospace has resorted to since the industry was hit by recession in the early '90s.
A company spokesman said the Prestwick facility would continue to employ about 250 people, mostly engineers, on support work for existing Jetstream customers.
The end of J41, mainly used on small feeder routes, ends British Aerospace's 40-year history of manufacturing turboprop passenger aircraft in Britain.
The company said it has delivered about 100 J41 aircraft since 1993 to customers in Europe, Australia and the United States and had a market share of 20 percent.
